findings.summary: The guard is not on any production write path
findings.detail: The class only returns decisions; it neither mediates the side effect nor issues a capability that a write primitive must present. A repository-wide call-site search found no production invocation of evaluate() or consume(), only construction/export and tests. Call sequence: a filesystem, Git, or GitHub adapter calls its underlying write primitive directly, and CP-HI-01 is never consulted.
findings.suggestedFix: Route every enumerated write primitive through one trusted adapter that requires a grant bound to the exact operation and target, and make the unguarded write primitives inaccessible to callers.

findings.summary: Intrinsically MANAGED filesystem operations become DIRECT outside an existing repository
findings.detail: projectNatured is false for every FILESYSTEM operation when the target is outside a detected or registered checkout. Consequently evaluate({operation: MANIFEST_CHANGE, targetPath: '/tmp/new-project/manifest.json'}) or VERIFICATION_CONTRACT_CHANGE succeeds as DIRECT without a run, despite CP-HI-01 explicitly listing both as managed writes. FILE_MUTATION during PROJECT_BOOTSTRAP has the same bypass before git initialization or repository registration, contradicting §6 and the integration PRD's managed-bootstrap rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Treat manifest and verification-contract changes as unconditionally MANAGED. Add a trusted bootstrap/project-write operation classification so creation of a new repository cannot be mistaken for an independent artifact.

findings.summary: A dangling symlink redirects a DIRECT artifact write into a managed repository
findings.detail: canonical() uses existsSync(), which follows symlinks and returns false for a symlink whose destination does not yet exist. For /tmp/note -> /managed/repo/new-file, canonical('/tmp/note') remains /tmp/note and probeWorktree reports OUTSIDE, so FILE_MUTATION is allowed DIRECT without a run. A normal writeFile('/tmp/note') then follows the symlink and creates /managed/repo/new-file. This is a concrete CP-HI-01 bypass without a race.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve symlink components with lstat/readlink even when the final destination is absent, or reject unresolved/dangling symlinks. Bind the actual write to a safely resolved parent/file descriptor rather than reopening the original path.

findings.summary: DIRECT file-write grants cannot participate in the documented two-phase protocol
findings.detail: evaluate() stores only MANAGED grants. A permitted independent artifact FILE_MUTATION returns a DIRECT GuardGrant, but consume(grantId) always rejects it as unknown. An adapter that follows the documented evaluate-then-consume protocol cannot perform the §6.1 write; an adapter that skips consume loses reclassification and revocation checks.
findings.suggestedFix: Store and revalidate grants for every allowed write operation, including DIRECT artifact writes. Only genuinely read-only decisions should be non-consumable.

findings.summary: A revoked pinned run owner does not fence worker writes
findings.detail: authorizeSession() checks only that owner_session_id is non-null; owner_binding_generation and owner_role_key are never validated. Call sequence: an ACTIVE run is pinned to owner generation 1, that owner binding is revoked while a run/task worker binding remains ACTIVE, and the worker calls evaluate() with its own generation. The worker binding passes and the write is allowed. This violates §23.2's Revoked Owner Generation hard reject and permits late writes under an invalid managed-run owner.
findings.suggestedFix: Verify that the run's pinned owner role/session/generation is still the active binding, include that owner generation in every grant, and recheck it at consumption independently of the immediate writer's binding.

findings.summary: Mandatory branch and worktree claim checks silently disappear when the touched resource is unknown
findings.detail: GIT_LOCAL requests are accepted with repositoryIdentity alone, but when run_repositories has no work_branch/worktree_id there is no toplevel, so branchTouched and worktreeTouched are null and all corresponding claims are skipped. Separately, currentBranch() collapses probe errors to null and the same skip occurs. Call sequence: another run holds branch main, the authorized checkout is on main, and GIT_COMMIT is evaluated with repository identity only and no declared branch; the guard allows it. This contradicts §23.2's Same Branch/Worktree hard rejects and CP-HI-08's fail-closed probe requirement.
findings.suggestedFix: Require exact branch and worktree context for branch-affecting/local Git operations. Represent detached HEAD separately from probe failure and deny when a competing claim cannot be conclusively compared.

findings.summary: Grant consumption leaves an unfenced check-then-act window
findings.detail: consume() re-reads state, deletes the grant, records success, and returns before the side effect occurs. No lock, claim lease, transaction, or fencing token remains active. Call sequence: run A consumes after seeing no conflict; before its adapter writes, run B acquires the exact-path/branch claim or A's owner generation is revoked; A then writes with the already-consumed grant. The mandatory claim/revocation reject is bypassed.
findings.suggestedFix: Have the trusted adapter execute the effect while holding a resource-scoped lease or fencing token acquired before the final validation and released only after the write receipt. The write broker must reject a token whose owner generation or claim epoch changed.
